result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): Both answers take a clear conditional position and see that the office manager's day of setup is the real cost, so both offer to do the setup for the clinic. A goes further. It gives a concrete test (a measurable problem, someone who can sign, committed staff time) to separate a clinic with a real problem from one just collecting options. It also sets checkpoints, a decision date and written owners on both sides. B's success metric has no named judge or review date, and it only hints at filtering out casual lookers through a fee. Neither answer gives actual wording for replying to 'can we try it for free'. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): Both answers reject a blanket open trial and suggest the seller do the setup. B adds three checks to run before any trial starts (a measurable problem, a person who can sign, and committed staff time from the clinic), plus check-ins, a stop point, and a decision date. Neither gives actual wording to say when a prospect asks for a free trial, but B covers more of the rubric.
